title.en: The exotic moment: fishermen, salt-gatherer and war-makers

hook.en: If the world went quiet, what would change? The poet imagines a fisherman, a salt worker and even the makers of war each doing something new in that silence.

objectives.en: Describe the figures the poet imagines in the moment of silence
Understand the poet's criticism of war and destruction

narration.en: If the world went quiet, what would change? The poet imagines a fisherman, a salt worker and even the makers of war each doing something new in that silence.

title.en: The figures in the silent moment

body.en: In the pause, fishermen in the cold sea would stop harming whales, and the man gathering salt would look at his own hurt hands. Those who prepare wars against nature and wars with gas and fire, wars with no survivors, would put on clean clothes and walk with their brothers in peace. The silence brings kindness to nature, awareness of one's own suffering, and brotherhood.

points.en: War-makers: green wars, wars with gas and fire
They would walk with their brothers in peace

Let us map each figure and the change silence brings.

say.en: In the centre is the moment of silence.
The fishermen would stop harming whales: kindness to nature.
The salt worker would notice his own hurt hands: self-awareness.
Green wars are wars against the environment.
Wars with gas and fire end in victory with no survivors.
The war-makers would put on clean clothes, a sign of a fresh start.
They would walk with their brothers, doing nothing, in peace.

explanation.en: Silence would bring kindness to nature, awareness of one's own pain, and brotherhood.

body.en: Neruda criticises human violence against nature and against one another. He shows that wars bring a victory where no one survives, which is meaningless. A moment of quiet reflection could make people realise the harm they do and choose brotherhood instead.

problem.en: What will the man gathering salt do in the moment of silence?

steps.en: State the action: he would look at his hurt hands.
Explain: busy work had made him ignore his own suffering.
Link to theme: silence brings self-awareness.

answer.en: In the silence the salt-gatherer would look at his hurt hands. Busy with work, he had ignored his own pain; the pause would make him aware of how his labour hurts him, showing how silence brings self-awareness.
